precepts.text: They were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.
precepts.point: The holy seed was mingled with the strange people of the land. Northern kingdom should learn its own history with the same zeal as the south's.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people.” Ezra already showed that the holy seed was mixed with the strange people of the land. David gives the other side of it: “But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.” It was not just ideological, dummies, and some of the ones saying it went to seminary school and call themselves theologians. When you look up the definition of mingled, it goes into mixing, just like First Esdras. And they learned their works too.

So Hosea is talking about ideology, and it is also talking about the seed, like we just proved. Scholars know the whitening was both ideological and biological. “Ephraim is a cake not turned. Strangers have devoured his strength.” The cake not turned is the colours, light and dark: some of us light, some in between, some dark.

The strangers devoured more than the strength of the royal seed. Our strength lies in the Lord, the joy of the Lord is our strength, and the ideology cut us away from him. We cannot fight the United States; our countries cannot do any of that. It is time we come back to God. Strangers devoured his strength, “and he knoweth it not: yea, gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not.” Many of our older people are not hearing it; the gray hairs are upon them and they cannot accept it.

And this goes with Matthew 13 and Amos 9, especially for you northern kingdom brothers. Southern kingdom, learn northern kingdom history with the same vigour and zeal that we learn yours. If you are a fisher of men, you fish all the different kinds of fish that pertain to Israel and Christ.

precepts.text: They soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the desert.
precepts.point: The psalm gives the depth of it: they soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, they made a calf in Horeb and changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass, and they forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

precepts.why:
Aaron told Moses, “thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief.” The psalm gives the depth of it: “They soon forgat his works; they waited not for his counsel: But lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the desert.”

They would not wait for Moses to come down from the mount, and they would not wait for the Lord's counsel. “And he gave them their request; but sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the Lord.” That is the camp Moses came back to, deep in wickedness; and Aaron, left in charge, could not blame the congregation for it, for the charge has to be carried.

precepts.text: They made a calf in Horeb and forgat God their saviour; he said he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath.
precepts.point: The psalm gives the depth of it: they soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, they made a calf in Horeb and changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass, and they forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

precepts.why:
“They made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped the molten image. Thus they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass.” Aaron said, “I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf”; the psalm says what that calf was: Israel trading their glory for the likeness of an ox that eats grass.

“They forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt; Wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.” All of that so soon forgotten. “Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them.”

A leader cannot blame the congregation, the same excuse Saul gave. Moses, the leader who carried the charge, stood in the breach for the very people who envied him.

precepts.text: Blessed are they that keep judgment, and he that doeth righteousness at all times; at all times, not one day a week.
precepts.point: Words like testimony, righteousness, grace, and faith must be defined out of the scripture itself: the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Egypt means slavery, righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“Blessed are they that keep judgment, and he that doeth righteousness at all times.” At all times, not one day a week.

“And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God”. Keeping the commandments is what makes you righteous, and righteousness is kept at all times, the fringes worn seven days a week and not on the sabbath only.

Righteousness is defined out of the scripture itself, for the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.

precepts.text: They did not destroy the nations, but were mingled among the heathen, served their idols which were a snare unto them, and sacrificed their sons and daughters unto devils, and the wrath of the Lord was kindled against his people.
precepts.point: The wrath of the Lord was kindled insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance; that snare is why Israel is where it is now, scattered among the heathen and serving them.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
Moses warned Israel not to be snared by inquiring after the gods of the nations, saying, “How did these nations serve their gods? even so will I do likewise.” Israel has a history of following what the other nations do, and the psalm records the snare fulfilled: “They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them: But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works. And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them.”

They did exactly what Moses said not to do. Instead of destroying the nations, they mingled with them, learned how those nations served their gods, and served them likewise. It went as far as the very abomination the Lord warned of here: “Yea, they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils, And shed innocent blood, even the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan: and the land was polluted with blood.”

“Thus were they defiled with their own works, and went a whoring with their own inventions. Therefore was the wrath of the Lord kindled against his people, insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance.” That snare is why Israel is where it is now, scattered among the heathen and serving them. The Lord abhorred his own inheritance because his people inquired after the gods of the nations and did likewise.

precepts.text: They angered him at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes, because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips.
precepts.point: Thou shalt see the land before thee; but thou shalt not go thither.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
That selfsame day the Most High tells Moses to get up into mount Nebo, behold the land of Canaan, and die in the mount as Aaron died in mount Hor, “Because ye trespassed against me among the children of Israel at the waters of Meribah–Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin; because ye sanctified me not in the midst of the children of Israel.” The account is in Numbers 20, and the psalm tells how it went: “They angered him also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes: Because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips.”

The people angered Moses at the waters of strife, complaining and provoking him after all they had already seen, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes. They provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips: Hear now, ye rebels; and he smote the rock twice instead of speaking to it, the Rock we read about earlier in this chapter. That is how he sanctified not the Most High in the midst of the children of Israel.

So the sentence stands: “Yet thou shalt see the land before thee; but thou shalt not go thither unto the land which I give the children of Israel.”

precepts.text: The saints are the Israelites; Aaron the saint was of the tribe of Levi.
precepts.point: They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the Lord.” Aaron is called a saint, and Psalm 148 tells who the saints are: “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.”

The saints are the Israelites. Aaron the saint was of the tribe of Levi, one of the children of Israel, the people near unto him. And it was this saint, with Moses, that the camp envied, until the earth opened and swallowed up Dathan and covered the company of Abiram.

precepts.point: Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
Numbers 25 is the history behind these verses. Israel joined themselves unto Baal–peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking the Most High to anger with their inventions, and the plague broke in upon them.

Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed. That act was counted unto him for righteousness unto all generations for evermore, because he had zeal in the fear of the Most High.

precepts.text: Who will rise up for me against the evildoers; Phinehas rose up.
precepts.point: Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” Phinehas rose up.

When Israel had joined themselves unto Baal–peor and the plague was breaking in upon them, “Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed.” He answered the question of Psalm 94 with action, and it was counted unto him for righteousness unto all generations.

precepts.text: Phinehas' zeal made reconciliation for Israel and gave his seed the dignity of the priesthood forever.
precepts.point: Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“The third in glory is Phinees the son of Eleazar, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord, and stood up with good courage of heart: when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel.” This is the same standing up the psalm records: when the people had turned back to Baal–peor, Phinehas stood up, executed judgment, and the plague was stayed. His zeal made reconciliation for Israel.

“Therefore was there a covenant of peace made with him, that he should be the chief of the sanctuary and of his people, and that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever”. That is what “counted unto him for righteousness unto all generations for evermore” means: his zeal in the fear of the Most High gave his seed the dignity of the priesthood forever.

precepts.text: Take heed you be not snared to inquire after the heathen's gods; add not to nor diminish from His commandments.
precepts.point: They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them: But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.” The command had warned of exactly this: “Take heed to thyself that thou be not snared by following them, after that they be destroyed from before thee; and that thou enquire not after their gods, saying, How did these nations serve their gods? even so will I do likewise.”

“Thou shalt not do so unto the Lord thy God: for every abomination to the Lord, which he hateth, have they done unto their gods; for even their sons and their daughters they have burnt in the fire to their gods.” That is what Israel learned from the heathen: they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils and shed innocent blood, and the land was polluted with blood.

“What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.” Add not to his commandments nor diminish from them. Israel's own inventions, the works they learned from the nations they should have destroyed, were the snare.

precepts.text: The Most High hates all abomination, and they that fear Him love it not.
precepts.point: They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“The Lord hateth all abomination; and they that fear God love it not.” The sacrifices of sons and daughters unto devils, the idols of Canaan, the whoring with their own inventions: these are the abominations he hates.

They that fear him love none of it. Israel was defiled with their own works because they learned to love what the Most High hates.

precepts.text: Christ came not to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfill the animal sacrifice.
precepts.point: Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.” Christ came not to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfil the animal sacrifice.

So the law and the prophets still stand, and they agree. When the psalm says he gave Israel into the hand of the heathen, “and they that hated them ruled over them”, that is the law (Leviticus 26, Deuteronomy 28) and the prophets speaking with one voice. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing.

precepts.text: They that hate you shall reign over you; the law and the prophets agree.
precepts.point: Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“And he gave them into the hand of the heathen; and they that hated them ruled over them.” That is the law fulfilled to the letter: “I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.”

The law and the prophets agree. What Moses wrote in Leviticus, the psalmist records as history, and we live it today with the heathen ruling over us in our own communities, the legal system and the government.

precepts.text: The stranger shall rise high above us and we shall come down, brought low for our iniquity.
precepts.point: Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“Their enemies also oppressed them, and they were brought into subjection under their hand.” Deuteronomy describes that subjection: “The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high; and thou shalt come down very low. He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him: he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail.”

The stranger rises very high above us and we come down very low, brought low for our iniquity, as the psalm says: “they provoked him with their counsel, and were brought low for their iniquity.” He delivered them many times, yet this is where their provoking landed them.

Nevertheless he regarded their affliction when he heard their cry and remembered for them his covenant. That is why David prays, “Save us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the heathen”.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting.
